description: The shared route table. Route ids and deep-link paths are identical on all four platforms; only the platform binding differs. Every route must be reachable by deep link, because automation cannot rely on tapping its way to a screen — see launch-args.json.
rules: Route ids match screen ids in screens.json. A screen with no route is a component, not a screen.
Deep-link paths are identical across platforms. The scheme is per app (see app-identity.json) — usesmileid-sample-android://products, usesmileid-sample-ios://products, and so on.

Sheets are LAYERS over the screen that owns them, never destinations that replace it. Their paths stay in this table and stay deep-linkable — a link resolves to the owner's own route with the sheet open, so a flow can still drive and assert one. A sheet that replaces the destination beneath it leaves nothing behind its scrim, which is what Android shipped. iOS, Flutter and React Native present sheets over the presenter by construction, so only Android's cell has to name both halves.
The SDK flow is ONE route with TWO presentations. Same destination, different container.
Arguments are typed on every platform. A stringly-typed argument that only fails at runtime is a defect.

Dev-only shell surfaces are NOT routes in this table, deliberately. A component gallery or API scratchpad belongs to one shell, is not part of the journey the four apps share, and must not oblige the other three to build a counterpart. They still get a deep link under their app's own scheme, because reaching one cold is the only way a flow can drive it, and their ids use a dev_ prefix so the sample_ namespace stays the spec's. Android has one today: usesmileid-sample-android://debug/components.

routes.notes: The third-party notices, shipped in the binary rather than linked: Apache-2.0 §4 asks the notice to travel with the distribution, so every platform renders its own generated licenses.json instead of opening a URL. Reachable by deep link like every other route, which is also how a device flow gets to it without scrolling Settings.
Also the post-submission landing route — replace, don't stack (docs/architecture.md §4).
The owner's 'Consent Details Form'. Shown for every product, seeded from the active profile.
Only for products whose spec entry sets needsIdDetails.
ONE route, TWO presentations. The SDK owns everything inside it — the host must not model consent/instructions/capture/preview/processing as routes of its own.
Unreachable until a country is selected — the trigger is disabled, so the route must also reject entry without one.
Its path sits under /profiles but its owner is the products screen, the only place the avatar that opens it appears.

Reached from the settings PROFILE row — that row opens this list, not the active profile's own page. Owns the created confirmation, and owns the /profiles/new sheet, so a create from a deep link lands on the confirmation rather than losing it.
Titled with the profile's name. Its CTA activates the profile as well as saving the defaults, so this is also how a newly created profile becomes the active one.

Resolved before /profiles/:profileId so 'new' is not swallowed as a profile id. It layers over /profiles, which is where the created confirmation appears — so a link straight here now gets the confirmation too, where a sheet-as-destination lost it.
A debug affordance with no design frame. Deep-linkable so a flow can open it directly rather than reproducing a hidden gesture — the Settings row that opens it is debug-only, the link is not.

automationEntry.description: Automation drives routes directly rather than tapping through. Both mechanisms must reach the same route table.
automationEntry.launchArgs: see launch-args.json; the args resolve to the same route plus the same query parameters
automationEntry.rule: Every route in this table must be openable cold (process not running) and warm. Cold-start deep links are where argument parsing and state restoration break.

sdkOwnedScreens.comment: Screens with no host route BY DESIGN — the SDK renders them inside its own flow, so a route-vs-screen check will always show `consent` as unrouted and that is correct.
alsoUnrouted: processing — none of these are screens.json entries either; they exist only inside the SDK
